d: Loss of ovarian follicle function before age 40, shown by amenorrhea with FSH in the menopausal range on two occasions. Causes include fragile X premutation, autoimmunity, Turner mosaicism and chemotherapy.
Amenorrhea from slowed GnRH pulses caused by low energy availability, intense exercise or stress, with low FSH, LH and estradiol and a risk of bone loss.
The liver protein that binds testosterone and estradiol in blood. Insulin lowers its production, so insulin resistance raises the free, active fraction of testosterone.
The PCOS definition: two of oligo- or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovarian morphology, after excluding thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia and nonclassic CAH.

The FIGO system for abnormal uterine bleeding: structural causes polyp, adenomyosis, leiomyoma and malignancy or hyperplasia; nonstructural causes coagulopathy, ovulatory dysfunction, endometrial, iatrogenic and not otherwise classified.
An X-ray study in which contrast is pushed through the cervix to outline the uterine cavity and tubes; free spill into the peritoneum shows the tubes are open.

A framework that sorts amenorrhea by failing level: compartment I the uterus and outflow tract, II the ovary, III the anterior pituitary, IV the hypothalamus and higher centers. Failure of II is hypergonadotropic; III or IV is hypogonadotropic.

Menstrual blood trapped in the vagina behind an imperforate hymen or transverse vaginal septum. It presents at puberty with primary amenorrhea, cyclic pelvic pain, a bulging bluish membrane and a lower-abdominal mass.

An in vitro fertilization step in which a single sperm is injected directly into each egg. It treats severe male-factor infertility and is paired with surgical sperm retrieval when the ejaculate contains no sperm.
